question: A 58-year-old man with hypertension is also found to have a serum creatinine of 1.8 mg/dL, urine protein 2+ on dipstick, and an eGFR of 42 mL/min/1.73m². Which antihypertensive drug class is the MOST appropriate first-line choice?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Thiazide diuretics are less effective at eGFR <30 mL/min and are not the preferred first-line agent in CKD with proteinuria. They do not provide the renoprotective benefit of RAAS blockade.

answers.text: ACE inhibitor or ARB (e.g., ramipril or losartan)

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. RAAS blockers (ACE inhibitors or ARBs) are the preferred first-line antihypertensives in CKD with proteinuria — they reduce intraglomerular pressure, slow CKD progression, and reduce proteinuria. This is a compelling indication.
Beta-blockers are first-line in hypertension with heart failure with reduced EF or post-MI, but not in CKD with proteinuria. They do not provide the renoprotective effect of RAAS blockade.

CCBs are acceptable antihypertensives and can be used in CKD, but they do not carry the specific renoprotective and antiproteinuric compelling indication that RAAS blockers do in diabetic or non-diabetic CKD with proteinuria.

overallFeedback.feedback: CKD with proteinuria = compelling indication for RAAS blockade (ACE inhibitor or ARB). This is one of the most important prescribing rules in hypertension management.
Well done. CKD with proteinuria is a compelling indication for ACE inhibitors or ARBs as first-line agents. The renoprotective effect is independent of their antihypertensive action.
